question: Is Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green louder than Bethnal Green to Mile End?
norm_question: is liverpool street to bethnal green louder than bethnal green to mile end

answer.text: TfL's in-cab figures in FOI-1231-2425 put Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green (87 and 86 dB LAeq) above Bethnal Green to Mile End (83 and 82 dB LAeq), whereas our NO-GO phone check (mean +0.54 dB) does not rank the sections.

verified_claims.text: In TfL's in-cab measurements from 24 June 2024 disclosed in FOI-1231-2425, Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green recorded 87 dB LAeq eastbound and 86 dB LAeq westbound (listed as Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street), higher than Bethnal Green to Mile End at 83 dB LAeq eastbound and 82 dB LAeq westbound (listed as Mile End to Bethnal Green).

citations.quote: measurements were taken from within the train operator's cab.

verified_claims.text: Our pre-registered within-trip loudness check between the two sections returned a NO-GO verdict because one of the 11 placement-ok trips went the other way at -0.13 dB, with the other GO conditions also unmet (a mean within-trip difference of +0.54 dB, below the 1 dB threshold and inside the Voice Memos limiter compression, and level variants not agreeing in every trip), so our phone data do not rank the sections.

Our uncalibrated relative phone-audio mean levels were -18.66 dBFS(A) on eastbound Liverpool Street to Bethnal Green (6 runs) and -19.42 dBFS(A) on eastbound Bethnal Green to Mile End (6 runs), and -18.8 dBFS(A) on westbound Bethnal Green to Liverpool Street (5 runs) and -19.07 dBFS(A) on westbound Mile End to Bethnal Green (5 runs), which cannot be compared with TfL's in-cab dB figures.
